A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PS-loss study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, loss comparisons, ablations, zero-shot transfer results, sensitivity analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and reports additional structural-metric evaluations, zero-shot forecasting results, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes ceiling rounding to floor rounding for the frequency-search limit, estimated period, patch length, and stride. This changes the specified segmentation procedure in non-divisible cases, although the three structural losses, dynamic weighting, and combined objective remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether implementation or training runs changed accordingly.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven datasets for multivariate forecasting and the same ETT source-target pairings for zero-shot transfer. Added metrics, forecast lengths, and backbone configurations extend evaluation within these retained tasks rather than introduce new datasets, domains, or transfer populations.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds zero-shot comparisons using MSE-trained OFA, AutoTimes, and Time-LLM; Time-LLM was cited but not evaluated in v1. The original MSE, TILDE-Q, and FreDF comparisons remain. The runtime comparison removes DLinear and TimesNet, retaining iTransformer.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds DTW, TDI, and PCC evaluation beyond MSE/MAE. Appendix J extends zero-shot evaluation to horizons 96, 336, and 720 and adds LLM-backbone tests at horizon 96. Runtime measurement changes from milliseconds per iteration for three models on ETTh1 to seconds per epoch for iTransformer on ETTh1, Weather, and ECL. Existing dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses quantitatively test structural alignment and temporal distortion, and extend zero-shot generalization checks across forecast lengths and LLM backbones. Runtime analysis shifts from architectural differences to dataset scale. The original component ablations, sensitivity sweeps, training/test curves, and forecasting examples are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty estimates. Table averages summarize forecasting horizons rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds structural-metric and zero-shot results in Tables 8, 11, and 12, replaces runtime results in Table 7, and revises OFA entries in Table 2. For ETTm2 at horizon 96, OFA's reported MSE changes from 0.298 to 0.170 under MSE training and from 0.290 to 0.162 with PS. These unexplained table revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains. Table 1 and the retained loss-comparison, zero-shot, and ablation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.1 derives the complexity O(C T log T + C T + d T) from adaptive patching, structural-loss computation, and gradient weighting; v1 provides only empirical timing analysis. Section 3.3 also revises the integer-valued patching definitions. No substantial theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about patch-level structural alignment, complementary statistical losses, forecasting accuracy, and generalization. The added experiments support existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly interprets MSE-trained forecasts' lower ETTh2 DTW scores as requiring more temporal warping, using TDI to distinguish numerical alignment from structural distortion. The runtime discussion now emphasizes overhead across dataset sizes. However, its statement that PS consistently improves all three structural metrics is broader than Table 8 supports.

D1.justification: v2 documents the additional metric calculations, including its adopted TDI variant, and reports per-epoch training costs. Conversely, Table 2 removes the explicit input lengths of 336 for OFA and 672 for AutoTimes, retaining only a reference to backbone settings; this does not establish an actual setting change. Hardware, framework, and code/data access statements remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds forecasting and survey citations, including DUET, GINAR, PPGF, and LangTime, plus DTW/TDI sources, while removing citations such as ConvTimeNet, FTMixer, and TDT loss. The positioning of prediction-side patching against global loss comparisons remains unchanged. FreDF's updated citation represents the retained comparison method.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited wording and terminology corrections, alongside acknowledgments and proceedings information. The appendices reorganize computational-cost discussion, insert metric and zero-shot sections, and relocate generalization analysis. Most existing prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial result displays in Tables 8, 11, and 12 and restructures Table 7 from model-based columns to dataset-based columns with different timing units. Figure 2 corrects gradient-weight labels, and the generalization and sensitivity figures are relocated and renumbered. Existing ablation tables and forecasting plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new structural metrics directly test benefits that v1 supported mainly through pointwise errors and forecasting plots; additional zero-shot tests and complexity analysis also strengthen validation. These gains outweigh limited losses, including removed LLM input-length details and narrower runtime backbone coverage. The improvement remains qualified by Table 8's overly broad consistency statement despite DTW regressions and unexplained OFA result revisions.
